title: Wireframe explainer VO bed
prompt: Output: one WAV, 48 kHz / 16-bit / stereo, exactly 960,000 samples (20.0 s at 30 fps = 600 frames). Python + numpy/scipy only. Synthesise everything (no samples, no downloads, no speech). Fixed random seed (np.random.default_rng(55)). A 20-second dark, minimal explainer bed in F minor at 128 BPM (1 beat = 14.0625 frames; bars every 56.25 frames), built to sit UNDER a voiceover: keep 200 Hz-3 kHz quiet (pad and bells high-passed or notched there by ~6 dB). Frame 0: low mono sine-sub hit on F1 with a click transient. Bars 1-2: a sub pulse on every beat (F1, 80 ms decay) plus a ghostly airy pad (detuned saws, 2.5 kHz low-pass, very wide) on Fm9 → Dbmaj7 → Bbm9 → C7sus4, two bars each. Every 2 bars a sparse glass bell (FM, ratio 3.5, 1.2 s decay) plays one note of the chord, panned alternately. Frames 270-300: a 1-bar drop-out (pad only) for a narration beat. Frames 540-600: final bar, sub hit on frame 540, pad swells and fades to 0. No melody hooks, no drums brighter than the bells. Target low end 20-25% of energy, stereo side/mid ~0.3. Master: -14 LUFS integrated, true peak <= -1 dBTP (4x oversampled peak check), last frames fade to exactly 0. You can't listen, so verify: measure loudness and true peak with ffmpeg ebur128 (peak=true), check the exact sample count, confirm the energy change lands on each cue frame, check every note fits the chord under it, render a spectrogram PNG and inspect it. Fix and re-render until every check passes, then report the numbers.
notes: Dark F-minor VO bed at 128 BPM: sub pulse, detuned pad with ~6 dB cut in the voice band, sparse FM bells, drop-out at frames 270–300.
